sentences.text: JUDGMENT
The petitioners No.1 and 2

, have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation SCCH4 3 MVC No.3416/2022 for the death of Athaulla Jhan, who died in a motor vehicle accident said to have occurred on 24.05.2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 24.05.2022 at about 0.05 a.m., the deceased was traveling in a Truck bearing No.
MH16AY6916 , when this vehicle came near Revadihala bridge the driver of the bus bearing Reg. No. KA51AA7196 drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the bus to the said truck, as a result Athaulla Jhan died at the spot.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Karnataka Institute of Medical Sciences, Hubli, where postmortem examination was conducted and handed over the dead body with the petitioners.

entities.text: Karnataka Institute of Medical Sciences, Hubli
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioners have spent huge amount towards his medical expenses, funeral expenses, obsequies ceremony and transportation.
SCCH4 4 MVC No.3416/2022 Prior to the accident, the deceased was very hale and healthy and he was working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.40,000/ per month.
The deceased was the bread earning member in the family.
Due to untimely death of Athaulla Jhan, the petitioners put to great financial hardship.
The petitioners are the wife and daughter of the deceased, have lost beloved care taker.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ with interest.
3. After service of notice respondent No.1 did not appear, hence placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 has appeared through his counsel and filed his written statement admitting the issuance of package policy to the bus bearing Reg.No.KA51AA7146 and its validity SCCH4 5 MVC No.3416/2022 from 16.03.2022 to 15.03.2023 and liability if any is subjected to terms and Mehar Taj Banu vs B. Noorulla Khan on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60080098/
2 conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 being the owner of the bus had entrusted the vehicle to the drive to be driven in a public place without a valid certificate and fitness and permit.

Further submitted that, the driver of the truck bearing Reg. No. MH16AY 6916 is also involved in the accident and he has contributed negligence by driving the vehicle in the middle of the road unmindfully.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the claim petition.

4. The following issues are framed :
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, de ceased Athulla Jhan died in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 24.05.2022 at about 5.00 a.m., on Hubballi Dharwad Highway, Dhar wad due to the rash and negligence SCCH4 6 MVC No.3416/2022 driving of the bus bearing Reg. No. KA 51AA7146 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs and dependants of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 8.
Advocate for respondent has submitted no evidence on their behalf.
6. I have heard the arguments of counsel for petitioner.
7. My findings on the above points are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per the final orders

for the following:

 ISSUE NO.1 :
 8.

3 produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar with sketch, Charge sheet,
IMV report and PM Report which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.

sentences.text: On going through the documents, one Hanumanthappa has lodged complaint with North Traffic Police Station, Hubbali, on 24.05.2022.

As per the complaint on the same day at about 00.05 a.m., the complainant, his father Hanumanthappa, and other persons were traveling in a tractor bearing engine No. KA25TR5282,as loader and unloader of Mango nuts.

After unloading the Mango nuts they were returning in the tractor towards their native, while they reached near Revadihal bridge the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA51AA7146 which belonging to National Transport Company drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and after SCCH4 8 MVC No.3416/2022 overtaking the tractor mentioned above, the bus driver lost control over the bus and dashed against the truck
, thereafter the bus fell on the tractor wherein the complainant and his father were traveling.
The bus driver B.Nagaraju and 5 passengers and truck driver, totally 7 persons are died at the spot.
9. Upon receiving complaint, the police have registered FIR against the driver of the deceased Nagaraju.
As per the PM report Athaulla Khan s/o Ahamed Khan is died due to respiratory failure coupled with shock and haemorrhage as a result of injuries sustained.
The injuries found on the dead body of the Athaulla Khan are also mentioned in the PM report.
10. The police, during investigation have also visited the place of the alleged accident and drawn spot mahazar as well as sketch wherein noted the place of the accident.

The jurisdictional police after completion of SCCH4 9 MVC No.3416/2022 investigation have submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 Nagaraju.B who is died in the accident and also against the accused No.2 Akshay Chitale, for the offences punishable under section 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC R/w Section 3,
181 and 185 of MV Act.
As per the charge sheet the accused No.2 did not possess the valid driving but he had only driving license to drive the LMV and he was also consumed Alcohol at the time of the accident.
Hence, the police have filed charge sheet under section 3, 181 and 185 of MV Act against the accused No.2.
In the claim petition it is mentioned that deceased was a truck driver but as per the charge sheet deceased Athaulla Khan was traveling in the bus stated above and he died in the said accident.
Hence it is considered that deceased was a passenger in the bus involved in the accident.
The respondents did not adduce rebuttal evidence.
The respondent No.1 do not dispute the accident and death of Athaulla Khan in the said accident.

12. According to the respondent No.2, the vehicle in question had no valid effective driving license at all, either temporary or permanent as on the date of the alleged accident and the driver of the truck has contribute the negligence.

But to prove this Mehar Taj Banu vs B. Noorulla Khan on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60080098/
4 fact the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

sentences.text: But as per the driving license produced under Ex.P.7 the deceased has valid driving license to drive LMV.
However, as per the charge sheet the deceased was a passenger of the bus.
So, the contention of the respondent is not relevant .
13. The standard of proof in the petition like the present is probability of preponderance.

The oral as well as documentary evidence of petitioners have gone SCCH4 11 MVC No.3416/2022 unchallenged and it is prove that Athualla Khan died due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA51AA7196 in RTA took place on 24.05.2022 and the said bus belonging to respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
14.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Athaulla Khan, died due to the injuries sustained in RTA dated 24.05.2022, which is caused by the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1.
15.
As contended in the petition the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased Athaulla Khan.
The petitioners to prove their relationship, with the deceased Athaulla Khan, have produced notarized copies Aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 and 2 and Driving License of the deceased.
These documents are marked at Ex.P.7 and 8.
The original SCCH4 12 MVC No.3416/2022 documents of the notarized copies are also compared, during the course of evidence and found correct.
As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased Athaulla Khan.
These documents are not disproved by the respondents.

In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners being the wife and daughter of the deceased, are the dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3 :
16.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
The accident took place on 24.05.2022.

As per Ex.P.7 Driving License the date of birth of the deceased Athaulla Khan is mentioned as 17.02.1972, that means SCCH4 13 MVC No.3416/2022 as on the date of the accident deceased was aged 50 years.
17. As stated in the petition the deceased was working as Driver and he was earning Rs.40,000/per month.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income of the deceased was Rs.15,500/ in the year 2022, then the annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 13.
The future loss of income is Rs.24,18,000/.

Since the deceased has left his wife and daughter, it is considered that, there are two dependents of deceased, hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal Mehar Taj Banu vs B. Noorulla Khan on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60080098/
5 expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.16,12,000/ (Rs.15,500/ X 12 X 13=
Rs.24,18,000/ minus 1/3rd = Rs.8,06,000/).

sentences.text: SCCH4 14 MVC No.3416/2022

18 . In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others),
the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was selfemployed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

entities.text: Kirti and Another etc., V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Once notional income is determined, the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do not take place in the domain of work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant,
J., in his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654: Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)".
SCCH4 16 MVC No.3416/2022 20.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the above decision, 10% of notional income should be added to total loss of dependency,
to the age of deceased, which will be Rs.1,61,200/.
21.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are the wife and daughter of the deceased.

Hence I inclined to award a sum of Rs.44,000/ for loss of consortium. Rs.27,500/ towards loss of love and affection,
Rs.16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/ towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
22.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 16,12,000/

23.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
the respondent No.2 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:
24.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.18,77,700/
(Rupees eighteen lakh seventy seven SCCH4 18 MVC No.3416/2022 thousand seven hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of compensation awarded to petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% shall be released to them and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/.
Draw the award accordingly.

(Rupees eighteen lakh seventy seven SCCH4 18 MVC No.3416/2022 thousand seven hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of compensation awarded to petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% shall be released to them and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
